db_evidence.notes: The DB and the agents' own tool calls give a clean fight boundary: event_steps row event_steps:00000541 (22170-22200) describes '赤尻马猴 appears with health bar; player fights with staff and sword', and topic_facts at time_s=22200 states 'boss 大猿 (great ape) appears with a damage value of -1600 on final blow'. event_chains explicitly names 'boss fights sequence (赤尻马猴 and 大猿)' as two distinct, sequential bosses, not one boss with a phase transition. Frames pulled directly from the source video confirm this visually: at t=22198s the on-screen boss name-card/health bar text still reads 赤尻马猴 with a partially depleted bar; by t=22205s the enemy on screen is visibly much larger, mid-attack, with a temple gate/scaffolding collapsing behind it -- a different combat beat consistent with the 大猿 encounter. The question's own clue_interval (22174-22238) spans across this boundary, which is misleading if taken as a literal search window: it covers part of the 大猿 fight too. So Immobilize, Pluck of Many, and Spirit (the 3 skills the reference credits) are retrievable within the true 赤尻马猴 window (roughly 22174-22200), but Rock Solid, which all clip_qa calls detect at ~22201.8-22220s, sits at or after the boss transition and is therefore correctly excluded by the reference answer.

root_causes: clip_qa window not clipped to the fight boundary the agent's own semantic_search/run_sql calls already surfaced (event_steps row bounding 赤尻马猴 to 22170-22200); every rollout requested a wider window (22110/22140-22230) that bleeds ~30s into the next boss encounter (大猿).

The visual sub-agent (clip_qa) identifies skill activations purely from visible VFX/animation cues and never checks the on-screen boss name-card/health-bar label to confirm which boss is being fought at each timestamp, so an activation used against 大猿 gets silently attributed to the 赤尻马猴 fight.

In rollout 3, the visual sub-agent additionally misordered the tightly-clustered early activations (Immobilize/Pluck of Many/Spirit all within ~3s of each other), showing that clip_qa's frame-level judgment is not reliably precise at sub-5-second granularity when multiple bright particle-effect skills overlap.

The question's clue_interval (22174-22238) itself straddles the true fight boundary (~22200), which may have primed agents to treat the full span as one continuous 'first fight' rather than checking where 赤尻马猴 is actually defeated.
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly used semantic_search/run_sql to locate the general time region (~22170-22230) and correctly identified the relative order of the 3 in-scope skills (Immobilize before Pluck of Many before Spirit) in 4 of 5 rollouts, matching the reference's 1,3,4 ordering exactly aside from the extra Rock Solid step.

The retrieval agents consistently escalated to clip_qa for this fine-grained visual-sequencing question rather than trying to answer from text captions alone, which is the right tool choice for this question type.

4 of 5 independent clip_qa calls (rollouts 0,1,2,4) agreed with each other on both the presence and rough order of a 4th 'Rock Solid' activation, showing the visual read of that specific event was reproducible even though it was ultimately out of scope for the question.
transferable_lessons: When a semantic_search/run_sql call returns an explicit start/end boundary for the entity/event named in the question (e.g. 'boss 赤尻马猴 appears ... 22170-22200'), clip the clip_qa window to that boundary rather than padding it generously; padding risks pulling in the next event and silently changes the answer's scope.

For 'in the Nth fight against X' or 'first encounter with X' questions, verify where X's encounter actually ends (boss defeated / boss name-card disappears / next boss's name-card appears) before treating a later timestamp as still part of that encounter -- especially when consecutive boss fights are chained back-to-back in the source footage.

When asking clip_qa to identify skill/action activations near a scene transition, explicitly instruct it to also report which boss/enemy is on screen (via the name-card or health-bar label) at each activation timestamp, so activations against a different target can be filtered out downstream.

Treat single clip_qa calls as somewhat noisy for sub-5-second ordering among visually similar bursts (rollout 3 disagreed with the other 4 on the sub-order of 3 skills packed into ~3 seconds); for fine temporal-ordering questions, consider a tighter, more targeted clip_qa window per candidate activation, or a second confirmatory call, rather than one wide-window call covering the whole fight.
open_questions: Whether the exact game mechanic is that 赤尻马猴 and 大猿 are strictly two separate boss encounters (as the DB's event_chains table labels them) or whether 赤尻马猴 could transform into 大猿 as a phase change within the same continuous fight -- if the latter were true, the reference answer excluding Rock Solid would need a different explanation (e.g. Rock Solid simply never being activated at all, only equipped/shown in the HUD, as several rollouts themselves flagged as a distinction to watch for).

Exact source-video timestamp at which 赤尻马猴 is defeated (health bar hits zero) was not directly observed in a frame; the 22198-vs-22205 frame comparison establishes the transition happened somewhere in that ~7s window but not the precise second.
